materials: Create a production GAME TEXTURE SOURCE atlas, exactly THREE columns by THREE rows, nine square panels equal size, edge-to-edge, NO GAPS, NO LABELS, no frame. Detailed restrained 16-bit painted pixel art matching the provided Rift Hunters game screenshot's crisp authored stone and wood texture language, but a medieval frozen outpost. Neutral unlit albedo, no cast shadows, no perspective, no 3D model renders. Rich but calm material surfaces with broad readable shapes and fine selective pixel wear, NO scribbled straight white lines, no noisy dithering. Muted desaturated blue grey and warm weathered brown, tiny soft frost edging, not neon. Top row left: old cold grey small masonry blocks, dark mortar and scattered frost at joints, seamless. Top middle: weathered vertical timber planks with subtle knots, chipped edges, a little frost, seamless. Top right: small staggered blue-slate roof shingles, a few thin snow rims, seamless. Middle row left: old dark forged iron surface with restrained worn edges. Middle middle: worn dark desaturated indigo wool canvas, fine weave and faded seams. Middle right: translucent-looking opaque blue-grey solid ice stone, sparse deep fissures not zigzag scribbles, cloudy center. Bottom left: glacial cliff rock with broad layered blue grey facets and snow flecks. Bottom middle: aged tarnished brass, mostly brown bronze, quiet centers and edge wear. Bottom right: perfectly tileable packed blue-grey snow/ice ground seen straight from above, midtone grey blue, small subtle patches of snow, sparse embedded small stone chips, NO long crack networks, NO objects, NO plants, no directional shadows. All nine panels need usable complete texture surfaces. Not a landscape illustration. Match the reference's level of detail, no grass in these new textures.
ground: A single perfectly seamless tileable TOP-DOWN GAME GROUND TEXTURE for a medieval frozen outpost. Detailed 16-bit painted pixel art, crisp square pixels and restrained shaped clusters, not flat vector. The ground is old packed snow over cloudy blue-grey ice. Broad quiet interconnected midtone desaturated blue-grey fields, a few soft-edged patches of pale compressed snow occupying only 25 percent, tiny selective marks at patch edges. NO high-frequency grain, no stippling, no confetti, no long white crack lines, no road markings, no large stones, no grass, no objects, no baked directional lighting, no gradient vignette. Calm and readable beneath detailed blue-white monster sprites. Entire image straight overhead orthographic material albedo, not a scene. Palette about 12 muted grey-blue colors. There must be far more quiet ground than tiny detail. Subtle variation in surface matters but no camouflage pattern. All four edges repeat exactly. A snow and ice equivalent of a beautifully painted RPG grass ground, at about40texels per meter with sparse refined detail.
